name: ATAN2
description: ATAN2 returns the arctangent of the specified x- and y-coordinates. It gives the angle (in radians) from the positive x-axis to the point (x_num, y_num), ranging from -π to π.
tldr: Returns the angle in radians to a point given by its x and y coordinates.

parameters.name: x_num
parameters.description: The x-coordinate of the point. NOTE: Excel lists x first, the opposite of the common math atan2(y, x) convention.

basicExample.explanation: The point (1,1) sits at 45°, which is π/4 radians. Note x_num=1 is given before y_num=1.

advancedExamples.title: Convert to degrees for a quadrant check
advancedExamples.scenario: Find the compass-style angle of a vector.
advancedExamples.explanation: ATAN2(1,1) returns π/4 radians, converted to 45°.

advancedExamples.title: Negative coordinates land in the third quadrant
advancedExamples.description: Both coordinates negative produce a negative angle.
advancedExamples.explanation: The angle to (-1,-1) is -135° (or -3π/4 radians), inside ATAN2's -π to π range.

howItWorks: ATAN2(x_num, y_num) returns the angle θ (in radians, from -π to π) between the positive x-axis and the line from the origin to (x_num, y_num). It uses the signs of both coordinates to place the result in the correct quadrant, avoiding the division-by-zero problem of ATAN(y/x). In Excel the first argument is x_num and the second is y_num.

howToSteps.name: Identify coordinates
howToSteps.text: Determine the x and y values of your point.

howToSteps.name: Press Enter
howToSteps.text: The angle in radians appears; use DEGREES for degrees.

limitations: Both coordinates cannot be zero; ATAN2(0, 0) returns #DIV/0!.
The result is in radians from -π to π.
Excel's argument order is (x_num, y_num) — the reverse of the common mathematical atan2(y, x) — which is a frequent source of sign errors.

commonErrors.fix: Ensure at least one coordinate is non-zero.

commonErrors.cause: Arguments swapped (y before x) by mistake.
commonErrors.fix: Remember Excel expects x_num first, then y_num.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: ATAN2 works identically in Google Sheets with the same (x_num, y_num) argument order.

faq.question: Why does Excel put x before y?
faq.answer: Excel's signature is ATAN2(x_num, y_num), which is the reverse of the typical math notation atan2(y, x). Keep this in mind to avoid sign errors.

faq.question: What range of angles does ATAN2 return?
faq.answer: From -π to π radians (-180° to 180°), covering all four quadrants.

faq.question: When should I prefer ATAN2 over ATAN?
faq.answer: Whenever you have separate x and y coordinates, because ATAN2 determines the correct quadrant, while ATAN(y/x) loses that information.
